title: On the Shortness of Life
author: Lucius Annaeus Seneca
blurb: Life isn't short — we waste it. Seneca's sharp little essay on time, busyness and living now.

luxury.e: A spa day felt like pure luxury.

cards.title: Life is long — if used
cards.text: We complain life is short, but we waste so much of it. Used well, it is long enough for great things.
cards.quote: life is long enough to carry out the most important projects
cards.qMean: Life is long enough if you use it well.
cards.qLife: Two focused hours a day can write a book in a year.
cards.cap: Adriaen Coorte - Vanitas Still Life with skull and hourglass · public domain

cards.title: Where time leaks
cards.text: Luxury and carelessness drain our days; we only notice at the end how fast it slipped away.
cards.quote: when it all runs to waste through luxury and carelessness
cards.qMean: Time disappears through comfort and carelessness.
cards.qLife: Hours vanishing into scrolling on the sofa.
cards.cap: A coronation banquet, 18th century · public domain

cards.title: Busy, but life is hurrying
cards.text: Busy people keep postponing living. Meanwhile life rushes on, and death won't wait for their schedule.
cards.quote: you are busy, but life is hurrying on
cards.qMean: While you're busy, life passes quickly.
cards.cap: Manuel Domínguez, The Death of Seneca · public domain

cards.title: Nobody owns himself
cards.text: Everyone gives their time to others — clients, cases, crowds — but no one claims time for himself.
cards.quote: no one lays claim to his own self, every one wastes his time over some one else.
cards.qMean: People give all their time to others and none to themselves.
cards.qLife: Answering every message instantly but never having an hour for yourself.
cards.cap: Johannes Lingelbach, Roman Street Scene · public domain
